source: Fux, The Study of Counterpoint (trans. Mann, 1965), pp. 31-32, Fig. 6: first species, counterpoint below, as Joseph wrote it, with the two mistakes Aloys marks
transcription: Sounding pitches as MIDI numbers (the counterpoint's treble-8 clef sounds an octave down), durations in beats. Fux's figures: 5 3 5 6 10 10 10 5 3 3 1. Bar 1 starts on G (out of the mode); bar 2 to 3 goes from a third to a fifth in direct motion (a hidden fifth). Fux's corrections: D an octave below at bar 1, and the low D held into bar 2 (a tenth), so bar 3 is reached by contrary motion.
